messages:
anya: quick sanity check thread — ran a short head-to-head between gpt-open-7b-q4 and gpt-open-7b-fp16 on the replay harness. saw ~12% worse p50 on the q4 path. digging into kernel selection + kv warm/cold behavior. attaching short notes below.

samir: can you paste the exact decode params + stop sequences you used? small differences there can change effective token lengths and kernel paths.

anya: sure. used the replay harness with these flags:
```
python tools/replay_harness.py --model gpt-open-7b-q4 --replay data/replays/assist_small.json --batch 8 --max-tokens 256 --decode "top_p=0.92,top_k=40,temp=0.2" --stop "\u201c\n"
```
same for fp16 run but model name swapped.

pj: did you ensure tokenizer alignment? q4 build uses the revamped tokenizer fastpath we landed last quarter, might split differently around weird punctuation / stop tokens.

li: i grep'd a couple of the replay prompts — there are a few long trailing spaces and unicode quotes. those can shift stop detection by 1-2 tokens which changes decode loop length and can flip kernel selection for the final decode step.

anya: good catch. i re-ran with a forced normalize step (strip trailing whitespace, normalize quotes) and the p50 gap dropped to ~6%. still nontrivial though.

bench-bot: summary (short local harness run, 1000 reqs):
- gpt-open-7b-fp16: p50=72.8ms p95=148.2ms p99=204.9ms qps=385
- gpt-open-7b-q4:   p50=81.6ms p95=153.9ms p99=218.7ms qps=338
(delta measured on same host, same seed, synthetic dispatch ordering preserved)

pj: that p99 delta looks larger than p50 delta; smells like cold-kv misses or occasional kernel fallback to slower path. can you share a perf sample trace (nvprof/ncu or our tracer) for a few slow requests?

anya: attaching a small clipped trace here — pasted hotspots:
```
[hotspots]
attention_matmul_kernel_generic  42%  (slow requests)
attention_matmul_kernel_opt     12%  (fast requests)
kv_cache_read_lock             8%
decode_loop_overhead           6%
other                          32%
```

li: interesting — the generic attention kernel shows up only when sequence length after tokenization crosses 128 in our kernel selector thresholds. Did the replay include some prompts that expanded token count due to emoji/unicode?

anya: yes, a handful did. i also noticed the kernel selector currently uses a heuristic that picks optimized matmul only for seq<=128 and head dim alignments multiples of 32. q4 quant has different head packing so more often misses alignment.

samir: so two hypotheses: (1) tokenizer differences causing effective seq length shifts, (2) kernel selector alignment/misalignment with q4 layout. to isolate, we should run: (A) same tokenized inputs feeding both kernels (i.e., force tokenizer output), (B) force kernel override to opt path for q4 and see perf/regression.

olivia: i can run (A) quickly by dumping token ids from fp16 run and feeding them into the q4 runtime (bypass tokenization). will report in ~30m.

anya: also repro'd a subtle perf regression when batching heuristics pick batch=16 vs batch=8 under burst load — tons of packing/unpacking overhead for q4 path. patch candidate: avoid re-packing if quant format matches.

pj: file a small perf-check PR with a benchmark mode to force no-repack; we can validate throughput/latency tradeoffs. cc @eng-runtime.

olivia: quick result from (A): feeding identical token ids into q4 runtime reduced p50 gap to ~2% and p99 gap to ~4%. so tokenizer alignment was the main contributor.

anya: excellent. that points to differences in tokenization and some stop-seq edgecases. still want to fix selector heuristics so q4 quantized kernels don't unnecessarily fall back when head packing is compatible.

samir: agree. next actions:
- li: add a tokenizer-normalize stage to replay harness and a regression test that diffs token ids across model variants. (owner: li)
- pj: add a kernel-selector unit test that throws a deterministic set of seq lengths/head dims and asserts opt kernel chosen when possible. (owner: pj)
- anya: bench with forced no-repack path under realistic burst patterns (synthetic + replay) and post a perf table. (owner: anya)

li: i'll add the normalize step and a small fuzz corpus of tricky unicode/whitespace cases to the replay suite. will PR today.

pj: will prepare selector unit tests and add a debug flag to force kernel path selection for local runs.

anya: i'll run the no-repack experiments and also capture KV warm vs cold deltas (i suspect cold kv read lock accounts for ~7-10ms on p50 in some runs).

bench-bot: noted follow-ups + owners recorded. marking thread: perf-investigation. :mag: 

olivia: thanks all, nice quick triage. will follow up with raw token dumps and a tiny repro harness for the tokenizer edgecases.

anya: thanks — i'll post the final perf table and a short PR summary once done. :thumbsup:
